title: Year 12 Physics Module 7 – The Nature of Light
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Physics Module 7, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What type of wave is light?
Which scientist unified electricity and magnetism and predicted electromagnetic waves?
What is the speed of light in a vacuum to two significant figures?
Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the highest frequency?
What technique uses spectra to identify elements in stars and other sources?

categories.name: What evidence supports the wave model of light?

questions.prompt: What spreading of light around edges or through small gaps supports the wave model?
What pattern forms when two coherent light waves overlap?
Which famous experiment produces alternating bright and dark fringes using two slits?
What optical device uses many closely spaced lines to produce interference patterns?
What property of light shows that light is a transverse wave?
Which scientist proposed a wave model of light that competed with Newton’s particle model?

categories.name: What evidence supports the particle/quantum model of light?

questions.prompt: What name is given to a quantum, or packet, of light energy?
Which scientist proposed that electromagnetic energy is quantised?
What effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency shines on it?
What minimum energy is required to remove an electron from a metal surface?
According to the photon model, what happens to photon energy as frequency increases?
What type of radiation spectrum led Planck to introduce energy quanta?

categories.name: How does light affect time, space and matter?

questions.prompt: According to special relativity, is the speed of light in a vacuum the same for all inertial observers?
What effect makes a moving clock appear to run more slowly to a stationary observer?
What effect makes an object moving relative to an observer appear shorter along its direction of motion?
What high-speed particles reaching Earth’s surface provide evidence for relativistic time dilation?
What equation expresses mass–energy equivalence?
Can an object with non-zero rest mass be accelerated to the speed of light in a vacuum?

finalRound.prompt: What two complementary models are required to explain the full range of observed behaviour of light?
finalRound.answer: Wave and particle models. Accept: wave and quantum/photon models.
